answer: Each agent identity requires a bonded stake of 50 timber units locked in escrow, verifiable against a one-per-hardware credential issued by the grove registry. An attacker forging N identities locks 50N units and, on detection, loses 100 percent of the bond after a 30-epoch challenge window, with the comet probe sampling attestations each epoch. Splitting identities raises marginal cost linearly, shared penalties drain the whole cluster, and independent jurors flag duplicated credential roots.
